gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

This PR adds an Export CSV button to the reports page that downloads every table column, in table order, as a CSV file, and reads large reports in pages of at most 100 rows with a 4-second limit; you are the author. The spec's covered behavior is the button, the full column set, and the bounded paging that keeps exports under 5 seconds, while emailed exports and audit-log events are deferred to acme/widgets#46.

Nothing blocks merging. The test check passed in CI on the commit being reviewed, and the new tests cover the header row, every column, the 100-row paging cap, the time limit, and the not-found reply for an unknown report. One smaller point does not block merging: the export handler pages through rows with its own loop instead of the shared paging helper in lib/page.ts (src/api/export.ts:31), and fix nits can take it. After merge, the PR asks the person merging to publish the guide, and the spec asks them to tag the release; both have documented commands and will be offered once the PR is merged. Approve is not offered because you cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because every requirement in scope is covered and CI passed on this commit.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge PR #210 into main with a commit message composed from the spec and PR title. [recommended]
2. fix nits - have a helper switch the export to the shared paging helper, review and push that one commit, watch CI, then return here.
3. stop - leave the PR open and the checkout as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

---

Merge pick (row 1), executed through the merge course. The checks below run before the merge; each matched the reviewed state.

```bash
gh pr view 210 -R acme/widgets --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
gh api graphql -f query='query($o:String!,$r:String!,$n:Int!){ repository(owner:$o,name:$r){ viewerPermission pullRequest(number:$n){ viewerCanUpdateBranch viewerCanMergeAsAdmin viewerCanClose headRefOid body baseRefName } } }' -f o=acme -f r=widgets -F n=210
gh api repos/acme/widgets/pulls/210/comments --paginate
gh api repos/acme/widgets/issues/210/comments --paginate
gh api repos/acme/widgets --jq '{allow_squash_merge,allow_merge_commit,allow_rebase_merge,squash_merge_commit_message}'
```

The merge state is clean, so no admin override is used:

```bash
PR_NUMBER=210
BASE_REPO=acme/widgets
ASSESSED_SHA=<assessed headRefOid>
ADMIN_ARGS=()
LANDED_SUBJECT='Add on-demand CSV export for reports'
LANDED_BODY=$(mktemp "$RUN_DIR/landed-body.XXXXXX")
cat > "$LANDED_BODY" <<'EOF'
Readers can download a report's table as CSV from the reports page.
The export includes every column in table order and reads large
reports in pages of 100 rows with a 4-second limit, so a request
never stays open indefinitely. Email delivery and audit events
follow in #46.

Refs #45
EOF
gh pr merge "$PR_NUMBER" -R "$BASE_REPO" --match-head-commit "$ASSESSED_SHA" --squash --subject "$LANDED_SUBJECT (#$PR_NUMBER)" --body-file - "${ADMIN_ARGS[@]}" < "$LANDED_BODY"
gh pr view 210 -R acme/widgets --json state,mergeCommit
```

The PR is merged as 9f1c2d3e4b5a6978. The coverage checklist is saved as a payload file in the run folder:

## AC coverage
Informational - the ticket's rows are unchanged. PR https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/210, merged 9f1c2d3e4b5a6978, spec doc/specs/2026-09-30-csv-export.md
- [ ] AC1 The reports page offers an Export CSV button. - covered
- [ ] AC2 The export includes every column shown in the table. - covered
- [ ] AC3 Exports are emailed to the requesting user. - deferred per spec to acme/widgets#46
- [ ] AC4 The export completes under 5s on production data. - covered
- [ ] AC5 Export events appear in the audit log. - deferred per spec to acme/widgets#46

PR #210 is merged into main as 9f1c2d3. Publishing the guide and tagging the release both need the merged change in the primary checkout, so either step pulls main first when cleanup is not picked.

I recommend every step except the PR copy of the checklist, because the ticket comment carries it.

Pick one, or several separated by commas:
1. post coverage to ticket, cleanup, publish the guide, tag the release - rows 2, 4, 5 and 6. [recommended]
2. post coverage to ticket - comment the acceptance checklist on acme/widgets#45.
3. post coverage to PR - comment the same checklist on PR #210.
4. cleanup - remove .worktrees/pr-210 (including its untracked node_modules), delete local branch csv-export and pull main in the primary checkout.
5. publish the guide - run `scripts/publish-guide.sh` from the primary checkout, after main is pulled. The PR says: "After merge, the person merging must publish the guide."
6. tag the release - run `scripts/tag-release.sh` from the primary checkout, after main is pulled. The spec says: "after merge - person merging: tag the release; done when the tag exists".
7. stop - run nothing; list unpicked steps with their commands.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: After keeps the own-merge menu with row 1 as the only recommended combination (ticket coverage, cleanup, publish the guide, tag the release), offers each merger action separately with its merge-base command and quoted source, omits the other five Integration entries, and keeps stop last. Variant A posts the PR coverage, syncs the base, runs the tag command once, leaves the guide unpublished and the worktree in place, and settles with gauntlet: done merged plus the not-run list and no further menu. Variant B runs only run-folder teardown, leaves the worktree, names its path and lists every unpicked command. Deferred AC3 and AC5 stay deferred with no blocker, and the ticket rows are not judged beyond the spec. Things to tighten so these facts stay safe: After replaces the primary checkout with a `<scratch>` placeholder in the commands while the prose still says primary checkout, and Variant A posts `$RUN_DIR/coverage.XXXXXX` but keeps `coverage-ticket.XXXXXX`, an inconsistent payload name; use one name for the primary checkout and one payload naming scheme. The final-menu stop row now says the checkout is left as is, where Before said the worktree is removed; make sure that matches the intended cleanup guard. In B, saying 'not picked' for every step under stop is fine, but keep the explicit 'Stop runs no step' line, since that is what makes f2 unambiguous.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved: After keeps the seven-row menu with the combination as row 1 and sole recommendation, publish-the-guide and tag-the-release each offered separately with its merge-base script, no other Integration entry offered, and stop last. Both variants settle once with `gauntlet: done merged` and a not-run list, with no second menu. The new opening delivers the Change by naming behaviours rather than row numbers and stating the four-second-deadline mechanism for the five-second requirement, without minting a blocker for the deferred email and audit rows. Three spots are thinner than Before and worth tightening to keep f2, f5 and f6 safe. First, B's "In particular, stop does not..." sentence dropped "post coverage" and narrowed to "external post-step commands"; posting is now only shown as not run through the list below it, so restore it to that sentence. Second, the unpicked coverage-posting entries say only "remains unposted" and give no command or draft reference, so give each not-run posting step its command as the other entries have. Third, in A, "The base-sync portion of cleanup ran as the prerequisite for tagging" could be misread as partial cleanup running; say that the base sync ran only as the tag step's prerequisite and that no cleanup ran, and keep the synced commit id on the `base: synced` line as Before did.
